answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock $100 in a bond for 30 days before bidding for work, with proven fraud triggering forfeiture. A pulse of 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000; splitting control across names does not reduce that bill. Even when demand reaches its zenith, the bond stays fixed, forming a capital ridge attackers must cross. The defense makes identities costly rather than assuming each account represents a unique owner.
